verification.notes: Award amounts by degree level, application windows, required documents and the two-stage selection (TU Graz expert jury pre-selection, then selection by the funding partner company) were read directly on TU Graz's own scholarship and Master's application pages. TU Graz publishes no statement on tuition, living or travel costs and no English proficiency test requirement; application documents must simply be in German or English.

applicant_utility.summary: TU Graz runs a two-tier scholarship scheme for its own degree students: up to EUR 8,800 for Bachelor's and up to EUR 17,600 for Master's, paid over up to two years, funded by named industry partners. The Master's window for the 2027/28 winter semester doubles as the nearest opportunity - it opens on 15 October 2026 and closes on 15 February 2027, so the work you do this autumn determines whether you can apply at all. Selection is not purely academic: a TU Graz expert jury pre-selects, and the funding company then makes the final call, which is why the motivation letter and reference letters matter as much as the transcript.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong Bachelor's or Master's applicants to any TU Graz degree programme who can show concrete professional ambition - a clear reason for choosing engineering at Graz, technical depth in a field a named partner company works in, and evidence of independent thinking. Applicants who enjoy fieldwork, workshops and company contact will fit the mentoring and educational programme better than applicants who want a purely technical, classroom-only experience.
application_readiness_checklist: Register for and submit the admission application to a TU Graz Master's programme for winter semester 2027/28 (admission itself is not required at scholarship stage)
Check the individual High Potentials scholarship list and confirm you meet each partner's own requirements
Write a motivation letter that names the specific scholarship and spells out what you expect from the partner-company relationship
Order the two teacher recommendation letters early - they must be on official letterhead and signed
Request a transcript of records and, if your degree is already complete, the Bachelor's diploma
If already studying at TU Graz, request a confirmation of your study period
Convert every document to PDF and upload before the 15 February 2027 deadline
common_rejection_risks: Applying after the window closes - the Master's window shuts on 15 February 2027 and the Bachelor's on 7 July 2027
Uploading documents as Word files or images instead of PDF
Reference letters without letterhead, signature or stamp, or written by someone who is not a teacher
A motivation letter that is generic and does not mention the specific partner scholarship
Skipping the partner-specific requirements for the chosen scholarship
Assuming the scholarship covers living costs or tuition - the award is a scholarship amount only, so you still need to prove sufficient funds
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: TU Graz publishes no coverage statement beyond the scholarship amount, so you must budget separately for the Austrian semester tuition fee, registration and Students Union fees, health insurance, rent, food and local transport in Graz out of your own funds.
applicant_utility.document_audit: Every document must be in German or English and must be a PDF. Build one folder named for the scholarship you are applying for, and name files in the form 'Surname_MotivationLetter.pdf' so the jury can find documents quickly.

verification.notes: Award amount, benefit list, formal requirements, full document checklist, age limits and the five-stage selection process (online form, full application, online interview, Grants Committee decision, notification in the first half of August) were read on AAI Salzburg's own pages. AAI states that the October 2026 call is closed and that the next call is expected to open in June 2027, and it publishes no living-cost or tuition statement and no English proficiency requirement.

applicant_utility.summary: The One World Scholarship pays EUR 500 per month during the semester (October through June) to students from Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East, Oceania, the Caribbean and Latin America who are enrolled in a regular Master's or PhD programme in Salzburg and pursue development-related topics. It is explicitly a partial scholarship, so treat it as a top-up on your own funds rather than a full funding package. Selection is heavily need-based: AAI looks at your income, savings, support, and your parents' profession and income, so the bank statement carries as much weight as the transcript.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Self-funded students from the Global South studying in Salzburg who can show real financial need, steady study progress, and an academic profile shaped by sustainable development - anywhere from climate and energy policy to migration, gender equality or human rights. Because attendance at a monthly get-together and the co-organisation of an event are expected, you also need to be genuinely willing to be community-active. Joint-Master students are only accommodated by arrangement, so this works best if you are on a standard Master's or doctoral programme at the University of Salzburg, UAS Salzburg or Mozarteum.

common_rejection_risks: Applying outside the call window - the current call closed and AAI expects the next one only in June 2027
A bank statement that does not match the declared income or that covers less than 3 months
Overstating need and failing the cross-check against your declared income, savings and your parents' situation
A transcript showing weak study progress
No demonstrable link between your studies and development or sustainability
Unwillingness to attend the monthly get-together or to help organise an event
Being over the age limit - note the 5-year extension for mothers
Using an incorrect e-mail address in the form, so that AAI's correspondence never reaches you
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: EUR 500 a month across October to June leaves the bulk of Salzburg's living costs uncovered. You still carry the semester tuition fee, the Students Union fee, local transport, food, rent of roughly EUR 400 to 700 per month, and your travel between home and Austria.
applicant_utility.document_audit: Non-German, non-English, non-French and non-Spanish certificates require a certified translation. Assemble passport, residence permit, admission and enrolment letters, the collective transcript of records, the bank statement and the CV into one scanned set so the transfer-link upload is a single action.
